- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
This is the third of four stacked PRs that introduces a simplified version of DSA. These stacked PRs split PR #[6869](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6869).
 
 This PR lets DSA indexer gradients be clipped under their own L2 norm, separately from the rest of the model. The indexer is trained by a KL objective against the attention distribution, and its gradients are roughly an order of magnitude smaller than the backbone's (in an 8B run, 0.009 against 0.108). Because clip_grad_norm takes a single global norm over every trainable parameter, the indexer's update would be scaled by a coefficient the backbone determines. 

To clip a subset of the parameters, the parameters are partitioned into an indexer bucket and a non-indexer bucket. The split is opt-in: dsa_indexer_clip_grad = None keeps the existing single-norm behavior, and any value enables two norms, with that value as the indexer's threshold.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `megatron/core/optimizer/optimizer.py` | `is_dsa_indexer` added to `param_group_identifier_keys`, with a `False` default so pre-DSA checkpoints still match; `get_dsa_split_parameters` and `get_dsa_split_grad_norms`; `clip_grad_norm_separate_dsa_indexer`. |
| `megatron/core/optimizer/distrib_optimizer.py` | Reuses the shared get_param_group_identifier_tuple instead of recomputing the tuple inline. |
| `megatron/core/optimizer/optimizer_config.py` | `dsa_indexer_clip_grad`. |
| `megatron/core/optimizer_param_scheduler.py` | Indexer learning-rate logging (`get_indexer_lr_for_logging`). |
| `megatron/core/optimizer/__init__.py` | Param-group plumbing for the indexer split. |

## Part of a series

This PR is 3 of 4 splitting a single 13k-line PR #6869 

| PR | Contents |
|----|----------|
| #7152     | min-memory DSA kernels (torch + Triton) |
|  #7156   | DSA-over-GQA attention layer            |
| **this PR**  | per-parameter-group optimizer clocks    |
| #7181   | indexer freezing, reset, checkpointing  |

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Issue tracking

For PRs from open-source community contributors:

- **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR.
- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Linked issue: <!-- e.g. Fixes #1234 / Related to #1234 -->

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

+def _tag_pre_split_param_index(params_map, params_key, model_order, key_order) -> None:
+    """Tag each parameter with the index it had before the indexer got its own group.
+
+    Torch identifies a parameter in a saved state dict by its position once the groups are
+    flattened in order, so splitting a group renumbers everything after the split point and a
+    checkpoint written earlier no longer lines up. Pairing the two needs the old number, and
+    it cannot be worked out when the checkpoint is read: the optimizer holds no reference to
+    the model by then, and the saved state carries integers rather than names.
+
+    Here both halves are available. ``key_order`` is the order the groups were laid out in,
+    and ``model_order`` is the order the parameters were walked in -- which is the order a
+    single group was filled. Collapsing ``is_dsa_indexer`` out of the key merges the groups
+    that used to be one, and sorting their members by model order reproduces the interleaving
+    of indexer and backbone parameters that the old group had.
+
+    Numbered separately for expert-parallel and dense parameters, because those go to
+    different optimizers and torch numbers from zero within each.
+
+    The index is written onto the parameter rather than onto the group, so it stays out of the
+    checkpoint: it describes the model in front of us, not anything that was saved.
+    """
+    collapsed = {}
+    for key in params_key:
+        collapsed.setdefault((key[0], key[1]), []).append(key)
+
+    for is_expert_parallel in (False, True):
+        subset = [k for k in collapsed if k[1] == is_expert_parallel]
+        next_index = 0
+        # (param_override_tuple, is_expert_parallel) ordered exactly as _key_order would,
+        # with the is_dsa_indexer element absent -- which is the ordering of the groups that
+        # preceded the split.
+        for collapsed_key in sorted(subset, key=lambda k: key_order((k[0], k[1]))):
+            members = [p for key in collapsed[collapsed_key] for p in params_map.get(key, [])]
+            members.sort(key=lambda param: model_order[id(param)])
+            for param in members:
+                param.pre_split_param_index = next_index
+                next_index += 1
+

+    "or start from fresh optimizer state."
+)

+def _is_dsa_indexer_identifier(identifier: tuple) -> bool:
+    """Whether this identifier names the indexer half of the DSA parameter-group split."""
+    return bool(identifier[_IS_DSA_INDEXER_INDEX])

+
+def _missing_param_group_message(identifier: tuple, saved_groups: Dict[tuple, Dict]) -> str:
+    """The 'no such group' error, listing what the checkpoint did contain."""
+    available_keys = '\n'.join(str(k) for k in saved_groups.keys())
+    return (
+        f"Could not find parameter group with key {identifier} in loaded checkpoint.\n"
+        f"Available keys:\n{available_keys}\n"
+        f"Parameter group key definition: {param_group_identifier_keys}"

+
+PRE_SPLIT_PARAM_INDEX_ATTR = 'pre_split_param_index'
+
+
+def _expand_pre_split_param_groups(
+    current_groups: List[Dict], needed_groups: List[tuple], saved_groups: Dict[tuple, Dict]
+) -> List[Dict]:
+    """Rebuild the one saved group into the several the optimizer now has.
+
+    A checkpoint written before the indexer split numbered its parameters over a grouping
+    that no longer exists, and torch matches saved state to live parameters by flattened
+    position. Handing each of today's groups the saved numbers of *its own* parameters makes
+    those positions agree again, so every parameter is given back its own state.
+
+    The numbers are read off the parameters, where ``_tag_pre_split_param_index`` put them
+    when the groups were built -- see there for why they cannot be derived at this point.
+    """
+    final_groups = []
+    for group, identifier in zip(current_groups, needed_groups):
+        source = find_saved_param_group(identifier, saved_groups)
+        if source is None:
+            message = _missing_param_group_message(identifier, saved_groups)
+            if _is_dsa_indexer_identifier(identifier):
+                message += _PRE_SPLIT_CHECKPOINT_HINT
+            raise ValueError(message)
+
+        indices = [getattr(p, PRE_SPLIT_PARAM_INDEX_ATTR, None) for p in group['params']]
+        if any(index is None for index in indices):
+            raise ValueError(
+                _missing_param_group_message(identifier, saved_groups)
+                + "\n\nThis checkpoint has fewer parameter groups than the optimizer, which "
+                "needs each parameter's index under the earlier grouping to pair the saved "
+                "state back up. These parameters were not tagged with one, so the checkpoint "
+                "cannot be matched; start from fresh optimizer state."
+            )
+        final_groups.append({**source, 'params': indices})
+
+    assigned = [index for group in final_groups for index in group['params']]
+    if sorted(assigned) != list(range(len(assigned))):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Pre-split parameter indices do not form a contiguous numbering "
+            f"(got {len(set(assigned))} distinct of {len(assigned)}); they do not describe "
+            "a single earlier grouping and would pair the saved state up wrongly."
+        )
+    return final_groups
+
+
+def find_saved_param_group(identifier: tuple, saved_groups: Dict[tuple, Dict]) -> Optional[Dict]:
+    """Find the saved group for ``identifier``, falling back across the DSA indexer split.
+
+    A checkpoint written before the indexer had its own parameter group holds one group where
+    there are now two. Both of today's groups were carved out of that one and had identical
+    settings by construction, so either may inherit it -- including ``step``, which the
+    distributed optimizer asserts is uniform and which a group matched to nothing would
+    otherwise restart from zero.
+
+    Returns None when there is no match even after the fallback, leaving the caller to raise;
+    the parameters themselves are never taken from here, only the group's settings.
+    """
+    group = saved_groups.get(identifier)
+    if group is not None:
+        return group
+    if _is_dsa_indexer_identifier(identifier):
+        pre_split = (
+            identifier[:_IS_DSA_INDEXER_INDEX] + (False,) + identifier[_IS_DSA_INDEXER_INDEX + 1 :]
+        )
+        return saved_groups.get(pre_split)
+    return None

+"""The numbering a pre-split checkpoint was written with.
+
+Splitting a parameter group renumbers parameters, and torch matches saved state to live
+parameters by flattened position. Reconstructing the old numbering wrongly is therefore
+silent: the count still checks out and training continues on some other parameter's
+momentum, with nothing in the logs to say so.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+
+# The ordering the groups were laid out in before the split, copied from _get_param_groups so
+# the assertions below describe the contract rather than re-using the implementation.
+def _key_order(key):
+    return (key[0] is not None, key[0], key[1], key[2] if len(key) > 2 else False)
+
+
+def test_tagged_indices_match_the_numbering_a_pre_split_run_wrote():
+    """REGRESSION: the tags must reproduce the old numbering when there are several groups.
+
+    With one pre-split group the ordering is trivial and any implementation looks right. With
+    two, the numbering depends on which group came first and on indexer and backbone
+    parameters being interleaved within each -- so this is the case that can actually be
+    wrong, and silently: a bad numbering still satisfies torch's count check and hands
+    parameters each other's momentum.
+    """
+    from megatron.core.optimizer import _tag_pre_split_param_index
+
+    override_a, override_b = None, (("wd_mult", 0.0),)
+    # Model order: the two overrides interleave, and within each the indexer sits between
+    # backbone parameters, as it does inside a real attention block.
+    spec = [
+        (override_a, False),
+        (override_a, True),
+        (override_b, False),
+        (override_a, False),
+        (override_b, True),
+        (override_b, False),
+    ]
+    params = [torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1)) for _ in spec]
+    model_order = {id(p): i for i, p in enumerate(params)}
+
+    params_map = {}
+    for param, (override, is_indexer) in zip(params, spec):
+        params_map.setdefault((override, False, is_indexer), []).append(param)
+
+    _tag_pre_split_param_index(params_map, list(params_map), model_order, _key_order)
+
+    # What a pre-split run would have produced: the same parameters bucketed without the
+    # indexer flag, those buckets in _key_order, each filled in model order.
+    pre_split = {}
+    for param, (override, _) in zip(params, spec):
+        pre_split.setdefault((override, False), []).append(param)
+    expected, nxt = {}, 0
+    for key in sorted(pre_split, key=_key_order):
+        for param in sorted(pre_split[key], key=lambda p: model_order[id(p)]):
+            expected[id(param)] = nxt
+            nxt += 1
+
+    actual = {id(p): p.pre_split_param_index for p in params}
+    assert actual == expected, (
+        "tagged indices do not match the numbering a pre-split run wrote:\n"
+        f"  got      {[actual[id(p)] for p in params]}\n"
+        f"  expected {[expected[id(p)] for p in params]}"
+    )
+    # And it must be a contiguous numbering, or the load-side check rejects it.
+    assert sorted(actual.values()) == list(range(len(params)))
